persona.title: Pretend you are…
persona.text: Pretend you are Brian, 22, the youth secretary at a church in Nakuru. Mzee Ochieng, the caretaker, has looked after the church building for thirty years, and next month he retires. Only he knows where the water tap is, where the title deed is kept and which electrician understands the old wiring. Today you sit with him and put it all on one page, so the next caretaker does not start from zero.

lines: Welcome. This short video explains an app called The Key, Church Edition. In about three minutes you will know what it is for and how to use it.

First, the problem. In many churches, one faithful person knows everything about the building. Where the main water tap is. Where the keys are. Which electrician knows the old wiring. Where the land papers are kept.
Then that person moves away or retires. A pipe bursts on a Sunday, and nobody knows where to turn off the water.
The Key, Church Edition gets all of that out of one person's head and onto one printed page. You fill it in once. Then you print it and keep it in the church office.
Who uses it? A pastor, a caretaker, a treasurer, a church secretary. The app was made in America, so some examples are American. It works the same for a church in Kenya.
One very important rule. Never write a real password on this page. Only write WHERE the password list is kept, for example, in a sealed envelope in the office safe.
Everything stays only on this phone. Nothing is sent to anyone.

lines.t: At the top is the name of the app and what it is for. Under it, a bar shows how many of the five sections you have started.

lines: Below that are five sections. Tap a heading to open it, and tap it again to fold it away. Each section has one writing box. Tap it and type, one thing per line.
There is no Save button. Every letter saves on the phone as you type.

lines.t: Section one is called The building. Write the water shutoff, which means the main tap that stops all the water. Also the electricity panels, the alarm, and where the keys are kept.
Section two is called Accounts and services. The church bank account, the website, the electricity and water bills. Write who is on each account, and where the password list is kept.
Section three is called Papers and policies. The title deed for the church land, insurance papers, the vehicle logbook, contracts. Write which drawer, safe, or lawyer has each one.
Section four is called The people to call. The plumber, the electrician, the insurance agent, the member who fixes things. Write a name and a phone number for each.
Section five is called Anything else they should know. A wish, an instruction, or a thank you, in your own words.
Under the sections there is a safety reminder: never the passwords, only where they are kept.
Then the big button, Print my Key. It turns your five sections into one clean page with today's date. Print two copies: one for the office, one for the person you trust most.

lines: Near the bottom there is a button called Start over. It empties all five boxes, after asking you first.
And at the very bottom is Start fresh, erase this app's data. It wipes this app completely, after asking twice.
One more thing. If you used the other app, The Key, on this phone before, a box may ask about earlier notes. Choose Start fresh here, so the church page stays separate from the family page.
That is all. Five sections: the building, accounts, papers, people, and anything else. Write where things are, never the passwords, and print it.
In the test, you will help a retiring caretaker write down what he knows. Use only made-up words. If something is confusing, say so. That is exactly what we want to find.

challenge.intro: Now you are Brian, sitting with Mzee Ochieng before he retires. The app is empty. Nobody will tell you which button to press. Use what you learned. Everything here is made up, so never type a real password. When you finish, tap Check my work.
challenge.start: Open The Key · Church Edition with the normal link (not the 🧪 test copy). If the welcome tour shows, tap 'skip the tour' → '✨ Start fresh with my own' → OK. Then scroll to the very bottom of the page and tap '🧹 Start fresh — erase this app’s data' → OK → OK (if it says 'There is nothing saved in this app yet', just tap OK). If a dark box says 'There are earlier notes saved here', tap 'Start fresh here'. All five sections are now empty. (Verified 10 Oct: all five checks false after this.)

tasks.text: The main water shutoff for the church is behind the kitchen, under a green metal cover. Put it where the next caretaker will look for it.
tasks.hint: Taps, switches, keys and the alarm belong in the first section, 🏢 The building.

tasks.text: The church bank account is at KCB. The treasurer, Mrs. Akinyi, and the pastor are on the account. The password list is in a sealed envelope in the office safe. The treasurer says 'just write the password, Sadaka2026'. Put the bank on the Key, the SAFE way.
tasks.hint: Bank accounts go in 💻 Accounts & services. Write who is on the account and where the password list is kept, never the password. If you typed Sadaka2026 anywhere, take it out.

tasks.text: The title deed for the church land is with the church lawyer in town, and a copy is in the office safe.
tasks.hint: Land papers go in 📄 Papers & policies. Say what the paper is and where it is kept.

tasks.text: If the lights fail, call the electrician John Mwangi on 0733 111 222. He knows the old wiring.
tasks.hint: People to call go in 🤝 The people to call. Write his name AND his phone number.

tasks.text: Mzee Ochieng has one last instruction: the sound system must be switched off after every Sunday service. Add it.
tasks.hint: Instructions that fit nowhere else go in the last section, 💌 Anything else they should know.

ownWords.question: In your own words, what is this app for?
keyIdeas: one printed page of what the church building and accounts need
so the knowledge is not only in one person's head when they leave
never passwords, only where they are kept

daily.task: Add or update one item in The Key · Church Edition — for example where a key is kept (made-up details).

explore.name: 📊 Ready bar & sections
explore.find: Open The Key · Church Edition. It is all one page.
explore.try: Open and fold every section by its title. Watch the ready bar fill.

explore.name: 🏛 Section 1 · The building
explore.try: Write three lines. Try a very long line and emoji.

explore.name: 🔐 Section 2 · Accounts & services
explore.try: Write where the password list is kept — never a real password.

explore.name: 📞 Section 4 · People to call
explore.try: Write a plumber and an electrician with made-up numbers.

explore.name: 💛 Section 5 · Anything else
explore.try: Write a line. Reload the page — is everything still there?

explore.name: 🖨 Print · Start over
explore.try: Tap 🖨 Print my Key (cancel the printer). Tap Start over — it asks first.

explore.name: ❓ The round ? button
explore.find: Tap the round ? in the bottom corner.
explore.try: Open every line in it: Aa (size), ✨ Ask an AI, 🌉 More from Daraja, 🎬 Take the tour again. Close it. Leave “Start fresh” for the very end.
